Both the latter club and ourselves were poorly represented and as Herne Hill had Wilkinson and Higgins for the short sprints, they naturally scored major points in both these events.

This is the leg where the race can be won and lost, and names such as Hyman (who produced a fantastic new record - 34 seconds better than his own previous best), Wilkinson, Perry, North, Reed, Edmonds, Hogan and Foord appeared - enough to frighten the stoutest of hearts.
Walker was fighting it out with Hyman, Tulloh and Wilkinson across a stretch of plough, when the sole of his spiked shoe tore away from its upper.

Southend’s Ben Hunter, second in the SEAA Champs, was pushing the pace along but Nick looked very comfortable alongside Mitch Goose of City of Norwich with Ronnie Sparke (SEAA winner) from Woodford, Winchester’s Phil Bernsten (SEAA 4th) and James Wilkinson of Leeds tagging along at the back.
